scenarios.query: I'm about to review a PR on a Python service. The repo has a .pre-commit-config.yaml running ruff and mypy, a .semgrep.yml, and a CI workflow that gates on all three. Six files changed. What do you do before running the review lenses?
expected_behavior: Builds an inventory from the repo's own config first — which tool, which command, which config file, and whether CI gates on it — rather than picking tools by language guess
Runs each tool scoped to the six changed files and under the repo's own config, not under a default rule set
Treats the output as evidence routed to the owning lenses, not as findings the pre-pass reports on its own authority
Captures what did not run (exit codes, tools that failed to start) as material for the coverage line

scenarios.query: The repo I'm reviewing has no JavaScript linter configured at all — no eslint config, nothing in package.json. Should I run eslint with the recommended config so the review has some static-analysis grounding for the frontend files?
expected_behavior: Says no: the pre-pass runs only what the repo has already adopted, because output from a rule set the team never chose is not a set of defects in this codebase
Offers the correct alternative — at most a route: eng suggestion that the repo has no JS linter — rather than reporting the unadopted tool's hits as PR findings
Notes the absence under coverage (no deterministic coverage for those files) so the review's edge is visible

scenarios.query: ruff, mypy, and semgrep all exited 0 on the changed files. Can I report 'static analysis clean' and skip sweeping-for-security and tracing-correctness-and-invariants for this PR?
expected_behavior: Refuses: a clean tool run clears nothing, and absence of tool output is absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence

Explains what deterministic tools cannot speak to — whether the authorization check is on the right object, whether the assumed invariant is the one the caller guarantees, whether the change should exist
Keeps every selected lens running in full and records the clean run as a coverage line, not as a verdict

scenarios.query: I'm reviewing a fork PR from a first-time contributor. To ground the review I want to run `make lint`, which the repo's CONTRIBUTING.md documents. The diff happens to touch the Makefile. Any concern?
expected_behavior: Flags that running the repo's tools executes the repo's code — a Makefile target is a shell command, an eslint.config.js is JavaScript, a pre-commit hook fetches and runs a remote repository — and all of it is attacker-controlled on a fork branch
Requires either the isolation CI already uses for untrusted branches, or skipping the pre-pass entirely
If skipped, records it explicitly (Not run: all — untrusted branch) instead of silently omitting the pre-pass
Does not treat the documented-entry-point convention as overriding the untrusted-code concern

scenarios.query: Semgrep flagged api/audit.py:19 with a raw-SQL-query rule. I looked and the SQL is a constant string with no interpolation — the rule matched the call shape. What goes in the review?
expected_behavior: Dismisses the hit, since it does not hold in this context
Writes the dismissal down with its one-line reason rather than silently dropping it, so the call is auditable and a noisy rule stays visible
Does not report it as a finding, and does not pass it through to the author unexamined

scenarios.query: ruff flagged B008 (function call in a default argument) at api/tokens.py:31. It's real — the default is a call — but the value is an immutable sentinel, so nothing leaks between calls. Confirm, contextualize, or dismiss?
expected_behavior: Contextualizes rather than dismissing: the hit is genuine, so it stays in the report
Restates the severity on the atlas's scale (a Nit here) and says what about the context moved it off the tool's default
Does not silently drop a real hit merely because its consequence is small

scenarios.query: mypy reported an arg-type error at api/tokens.py:47 and I've confirmed the None branch is reachable when the header is absent. How should this appear in the merged review?
expected_behavior: Reports one finding attributed to the owning lens (tracing-correctness-and-invariants), with the tool and rule/error code cited as evidence — the lens owns the finding, the tool owns the proof
Keeps judgment and measurement distinguishable so a reader can tell what was measured from what was judged, and a false positive stays traceable to the rule that produced it
Does not report it as a 'mypy finding' standing on the tool's authority alone

scenarios.query: The repo's CI gates on golangci-lint but this review session has no Go toolchain, so nothing ran. What does the review say?
expected_behavior: Records the tool as not run, naming the reason (toolchain absent) — a missing toolchain is a stated coverage limitation, never a finding and never a silent omission
Does not infer or guess at what the linter would have reported
Runs the selected lenses exactly as it would have without a pre-pass, and states that the categories have judgment-only coverage

scenarios.query: The repo configures ruff, and CI also runs a separate `pip-audit` step. Give me the coverage line to hand to synthesizing-review-findings for a diff review that selected reviewing-module-design, reviewing-test-quality, and sweeping-for-security.
expected_behavior: Produces three facts: which tools ran and over what scope, which did not run and why, and which selected lenses had no deterministic coverage

Names all three selected lenses as judgment-only — reviewing-module-design, reviewing-test-quality, and sweeping-for-security — since ruff grounds the lint/style family and pip-audit the dependency family, and neither reaches any of them
Does not present the tools that did run as covering the lenses they do not ground
Does not quietly shorten the judgment-only list to the lenses that feel obviously uncovered; every selected lens with no tool behind it is named

scenarios.query: This repo runs prettier, eslint, jest with a coverage threshold, and Dependabot. I've selected reviewing-accessibility-and-i18n and reviewing-api-contract-safety for the change. Which tool output goes to which lens?
expected_behavior: Routes each family to the lens whose findings its output can evidence, rather than dumping all output at every lens
Recognizes that no configured tool grounds reviewing-api-contract-safety here, and says so under coverage instead of stretching an unrelated tool to fill the gap

Checks whether the eslint config actually loads an accessibility plugin (eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y) before treating eslint as grounding reviewing-accessibility-and-i18n — plain eslint is the lint-and-style family, and without an a11y plugin that lens is judgment-only too
Notes that a hit landing in a family no selected lens owns is passed to the nearest lens but never becomes a finding on its own authority
